title: Path Traversal in Static File Handler - Directory Escape
description:
The static file handler at /static/ is vulnerable to path traversal attacks using unencoded relative path sequences. The request /static/../ successfully escapes the static directory restriction and returns content from the parent directory (the homepage). This occurs because the handler does not properly canonicalize or validate file paths before serving them.

The vulnerability allows attackers to use directory traversal sequences (../) to navigate outside the intended /static/ directory scope. While URL-encoded variants (..%2f) trigger a server error, unencoded sequences pass through unfiltered, enabling access to content outside the static directory.

Root Cause: The static file handler lacks proper path normalization and validation to prevent relative path sequences from escaping the designated static directory.
impact:
An attacker can bypass directory restrictions and access files/directories outside the /static/ directory. In this case, /static/../ successfully returns the application homepage (HTTP 200). This could potentially be leveraged to access sensitive files if they are served through the static handler. Combined with proper path sequences, an attacker might be able to:
- Access application configuration files
- Retrieve sensitive data stored in parent directories
- Map the application directory structure
- Potentially access system files depending on the Django configuration and file permissions

This vulnerability undermines the security boundary intended by the static directory isolation.
evidence:
POC execution results confirm the vulnerability:

Test 2 - Path Traversal Attack:
- Request: GET /static/../
- Response Status: HTTP 200 OK
- Response Size: 4467 bytes
- Response Content: Full HTML of Art Gallery homepage (containing <title>Art Gallery</title>)

Test 4 - Deeper Traversal:
- Request: GET /static/../../
- Response Status: HTTP 200 OK
- Both unencoded traversal attempts successfully escape the static directory

Test 3 - URL-Encoded Variant:
- Request: GET /static/..%2f
- Response Status: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
- Shows that URL-encoded sequences are processed differently (rejected)

This demonstrates that the static handler processes unencoded ../ sequences without proper validation or canonicalization, allowing directory escape attacks.
references: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'), OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, Django Security Documentation: Static Files
toolCallDescription: Document the path traversal vulnerability with confirmed POC evidence
